The Prophet kept I'tikaf in Ramadan's last ten days, his wives after him; Aisha combed his hair from her room during menses; Umar was told to fulfil his I'tikaf vow.
Seeing his wives' tents, the Prophet left I'tikaf until Shawwal; walking Safiya home, he told two Ansari men Satan runs in people like blood; a wife kept I'tikaf while bleeding.
The Prophet's dream of prostrating in mud came true in I'tikaf; he had his wives' tents removed; Umar fulfilled his vow; the Prophet kept twenty days the year he died.
Abu Huraira narrates more than emigrants busy trading or Ansar busy with property because he stayed with the Prophet, and after spreading his garment at his word forgot nothing.
Abdur-Rahman bin Auf declined his Ansari brother's offer of half his wealth, traded in the Qainuqa market and married; trade at pre-Islamic markets in the Hajj season was allowed.
Between clear lawful and unlawful lie doubts: the Prophet was wary of a claimed foster marriage, doubtful game and stray dates, but doubt breaks no ablution and forbids no meat.
People left Friday prayer for a caravan; a time will come when none cares if money is lawful; exchange is allowed hand to hand; Umar missed a ruling while trading.
A wife giving household food in charity without waste is rewarded, as are her husband and storekeeper; giving from his earnings without permission earns her half his reward.
Whoever wants his provision expanded and his life lengthened should keep good relations with his relatives.
The Prophet bought grain on credit from a Jew, pledging his iron armour, and said Muhammad's household had not a sa of food for the evening meal.
Abu Bakr, serving the Muslims, fed his family from the treasury; companions laboured by hand; the best food is earned by one's own hands, like David's, and woodcutting beats begging.
The Prophet asked Allah's mercy for one lenient in buying, selling and claiming his money; Allah forgave men who gave debtors time and forgave those in hardship.
Buyer and seller truthful about defects are blessed, while liars lose the blessing; bartering two sa of mixed dates for one is forbidden; an Ansari's butcher cooked for the Prophet.
People will not care if gain is lawful; the Prophet banned alcohol trade, dreamt of a riba-eater stoned in a river of blood, and forbade dog prices, tattooing and riba.
Swearing may sell goods but loses Allah's blessing, and a verse on selling Allah's covenant and oaths came down about a man who swore falsely to cheat a Muslim.
Planning to marry Fatima, Ali arranged for a goldsmith of Bani Qainuqa to bring idhkhir with him and sell it to goldsmiths to pay for his wedding banquet.
Allah made Mecca a sanctuary where fighting was allowed the Prophet only a few hours; its shrubs, trees, game and lost things are protected, except idhkhir for goldsmiths and roofs.
Asi bin Wail refused to repay Khabbab the blacksmith unless he disbelieved, mocking that he would pay after resurrection with wealth and children, and a verse came down about him.
The Prophet ate a tailor's meal, picking out the gourd, and wore a sheet a woman wove him, then gave it to a man wanting it for his shroud.
A woman's slave carpenter made the Prophet a pulpit, and when he sat on it the palm stem he used to preach beside cried until he embraced it.
The Prophet bought grain on credit against his armour and bought Jabir's camel, returning it with its price; trade in the Hajj season is allowed; Ibn Umar kept defective camels.
A good companion is like a musk seller whose scent you buy or enjoy, a bad one like a blacksmith's bellows that burns your clothes or leaves a foul smell.
The Prophet paid Abu Taiba a sa of dates for cupping him and had his masters lighten his tax; were the wage unlawful, he would not have paid it.
The Prophet sent Umar a silk garment to benefit from by selling, not to wear, since it is worn by one with no share in the Hereafter.
The Prophet would not enter over a cushion with pictures Aisha bought, saying picture-makers will be told to give them life and angels do not enter houses with pictures.
The Prophet asked Bani Najjar to price their garden; buyer and seller may cancel or confirm until they part, and truthful dealing blesses a deal while lies remove its blessing.
The Prophet bought Umar's camel and gave it straight to Ibn Umar, who left one deal quickly so it stood; a man often cheated was told to say 'no cheating'.
An army attacking the Ka'bah will be swallowed by the earth at Al-Baida', market people and others among them, and all will be resurrected and judged by their intentions.
Prayer in congregation is over twenty times better than at home or market; each step to the mosque raises a degree, and angels pray for one awaiting prayer.
When a man called 'Abul-Qasim' meaning someone else, the Prophet told people to name themselves with his name but not with his kunya.
Going by the Bani Qainuqa market to Fatima's house, the Prophet embraced and kissed his grandson Al-Hasan and asked Allah to love him and whoever loves him.
Food bought from caravans was not to be resold where it was bought but carried to the food market, nor resold before it was received in full measure.
Abdullah bin Amr said the Torah describes the Prophet as witness, bearer of glad tidings and warner, Al-Mutawakkil, neither harsh nor loud in markets, forgiving evildoers, and opening blind eyes.
Food is resold only once its measure is settled; measuring brings blessing; Jabir's measured dates paid his father's debts undiminished, and the Prophet prayed for Medina's mudd and sa.
Food may not be resold before being measured and received, and sellers who had not taken it home were punished; like-for-like exchange is riba unless equal and hand to hand.
When permission to emigrate came, the Prophet told Abu Bakr at noon, accepted his company, and took one of his two prepared she-camels only on paying its price.
The Prophet forbade luring another's buyer, town dwellers selling for desert dwellers, najsh, selling an unborn camel's young, and sales by touching or tossing cloth; he sold a man's slave.
Whoever buys a sheep or camel left unmilked may keep it or return it with a sa of dates; meeting sellers before market, najsh and luring others' buyers are forbidden.
A slave-girl proven to have committed illegal sexual intercourse is lashed by her owner without further blame, and after a third offence sold even for a hair rope.
Aisha was told to buy and free Barirah, the wala' going to the one who frees, and the Prophet declared conditions not in Allah's Book invalid even if a hundred.
